It positions itself as a solutions partner rather than a component supplier, bringing design, prototyping and production together under one roof and building customised parts to customer specification. drhp.one_liner: Permanent Magnets Limited is a 65+ year old Indian manufacturer of magnets, magnetic assemblies and current/speed sensing components supplied to electricity metering, EV and automotive, specialised alloys and industrial customers in India and abroad.

Magnetic Sensing: Speed sensing devices using Alnico magnets
Torque and angle sensing assemblies for EPAS/EPS
Relays (under development): Latching Relays (licensed from REL Developments Limited, UK)

risks.note: The MD's letter states the first half of FY26 was held back by lower exports business, particularly to the United States following interim uncertainty in tariff policy, making a material part of the revenue base sensitive to trade-policy shifts outside the Company's control.
risks.risk: Export exposure to US trade/tariff policy

risks.note: PML supplies primarily Western EV manufacturers, where demand held flat while Chinese manufacturers continue to gain share globally; the Company's response is to widen its customer base and product range, so the vertical's growth depends on that diversification succeeding.
risks.risk: Competitive share loss to Chinese manufacturers in EV/automotive

risks.note: The Company could not generate revenue from the existing assemblies business at subsidiary Quantum Magnetics this year because of restrictions on rare earth magnets — an external supply-chain constraint that directly removed a revenue stream.
risks.risk: Rare earth supply restrictions affecting the magnet assemblies business

risks.note: Management explicitly acknowledges being behind original timelines on Relays, with commercial ramp-up pushed to H2FY27 because customers require extended endurance testing before adopting a new supplier; the growth case for the metering business rests on this conversion.
risks.risk: Execution and timeline slippage in the Relays programme

risks.note: Domestic energy meter demand was softer in the first half due to certain customer-specific factors before recovering later in the year, indicating the segment's volumes can swing on the behaviour of a small number of customers.
risks.risk: Customer concentration and customer-specific demand volatility in domestic energy meters

risks.note: Consolidated results reflect the early investment phase at Quantum Magnetics, and further phases of investment are due in Q3FY27, so consolidated profitability will continue to carry the venture's build-out cost ahead of any revenue.
risks.risk: Early investment phase drag from the Quantum Magnetics subsidiary

risks.note: Standalone net profit growth in FY26 was struck after absorbing a one-time provision relating to the new labour codes, evidencing exposure to changes in statutory employment cost regimes.
risks.risk: Regulatory/statutory cost changes — new labour codes

risks.note: The relays opportunity is framed around the Government of India's RDSS smart-meter rollout, of which only 65 million of a targeted 250 million meters were installed as of April 2026 — the runway is large but the pace of the addressable market is set by a public programme.
risks.risk: Dependence on a government programme for the metering growth runway

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
